label: May 1917
headline: Ships in Convoy
deck: Merchant ships sail under escort; Australians take Bullecourt
caption: Steamers keep station behind a destroyer in the Atlantic swell
body: On 10 May a group of merchant ships leaves Gibraltar for Britain under the escort of warships and arrives without loss. The Admiralty, which has long held that convoys would only gather targets for the U-boats, now prepares to send ships across the Atlantic the same way.

In France the British attack at Bullecourt again on 3 May, against the Hindenburg Line. Australian brigades fight their way into the German trenches and hold them through two weeks of counter-attacks; the ruined village is taken on 17 May.
On the Isonzo the Italians open their tenth offensive on 12 May and gain ground towards Mount Hermada, the last height before Trieste.
On 25 May Gotha bombers attack Folkestone by daylight; ninety-five people die, most of them in a crowded shopping street.
briefs: The United States introduces compulsory military service
Kerensky becomes Russia's minister of war
Allied attacks at Doiran in Macedonia fail
